data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
RAF Fairford: Netanyahu claims Israel warned UK of ‘Iranian attack’
Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed Israel gave Britain intelligence about the incident last Sunday near the RAF Fairford military base, without providing any evidence.
The Israeli prime minister also suggested the British government has given in to an "Islamist-Marxist alliance", less than a day after an Israeli minister labelled British Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood an "Islamist".
In an interview with Fox News, Netanyahu said: "You talked about the thing in Britain. Do you want to hear how absurd things are there? And how far the anti-Israeli propaganda has gone?"
He added: "We gave the Brits the intel, that there was going to be an attack, and it's an Iranian-sponsored attack, and pretty much the next day they slap sanctions on us.
"It’s wild, the caving in, the collapse before the Islamist-Marxist alliance is very dangerous for the future of the West."

Manchester City faces potential legal action after a commission found it guilty of 115 financial breaches
Manchester City's Emirati chairman Khaldoon al-Mubarak (centre) attends the UEFA Champions League match between Monaco and Man City at Stade Louis II, in Monaco on 1 October 2025 (AFP)
Off
The Emirati chair of Manchester City, Khaldoon al-Mubarak, received diplomatic immunity in the UK in 2020, which generally protects individuals from criminal prosecution and certain legal proceedings in the country where they serve.
On Tuesday, the Premier League announced that an independent commission had found City guilty on 115 counts of breaching its financial rules by artificially inflating its finances by more than £900 million.
Mubarak is the managing director and group CEO of Mubadala, a $330bn sovereign wealth fund whose main shareholder is the Abu Dhabi government.
Mubarak has chaired City since 2008. In 2013, he received a Commander of the Order of the British Empire honour, partly for strengthening cultural ties between the UK and the UAE, including through the football club’s acquisition.
The investigation found that City’s owners had “concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators” to bypass spending limits between 2008 and 2018.
City have denied the charges, rejected the findings and said they would appeal. There is no suggestion that Mubarak has engaged in wrongdoing.
The club used "sham" commercial contracts to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than $1bn, the findings showed.
"The Club’s financial statements had not been prepared and audited in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory principles," the commission wrote.
It was "reckless" and "acted other than with utmost good faith", it added.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Seven killed in Syria after gunmen open fire on bus in Homs
data.author: Reem Aouir
data.summary:
Seven killed in Syria after gunmen open fire on bus in Homs

Attack on bus that killed seven civilians was one of several security incidents to hit Syria including a blast at a power plant
Syrian forensic investigators inspecting a civilian vehicle targeted on the Masyaf bridge in Homs province north of the capital Damascus (Handout/Sana/AFP)
Off
Gunmen in Syria killed seven people and wounded four others after opening fire on a civilian bus in western Homs province on Wednesday evening.
The bus was carrying company employees returning home from work when it came under fire as it crossed the Masyaf Bridge in the western Homs countryside, according to the Homs Health Directorate.
Security units were immediately deployed to the scene to secure the area, while criminal investigators began collecting evidence to identify those responsible and determine the motive, according to Homs Internal Security Forces commander Brig Gen Bassem Mohammad Shaaban.
The injured were taken to hospitals across the governorate, while security forces began an investigation.
Maan Mahmoud Fahd, director of the Homs Grand Hospital, told Sana that four individuals were declared dead upon arrival, after suffering from severe gunshot wounds to the head and chest.
No group has yet claimed responsibility, and authorities have not named any suspects.
Shaaban vowed to pursue those responsible, saying the attack would not go unpunished.

“We view this cowardly attack as an attempt to undermine security in Homs and destabilise the stability we have worked to consolidate,” Shaaban said.
“We will not allow criminals to threaten the security of our people or undermine the stability the city is experiencing,” he added.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Who is leading the race for 'the most impossible job on this Earth'?
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Who is leading the race for 'the most impossible job on this Earth'?
In April 1953, Norwegian UN Secretary-General Trygve Lie was at New York’s Idlewild Airport to meet his successor. "Welcome, Dag Hammarskjold, to the most impossible job on this Earth," he greeted the Swedish diplomat.
Seven decades later, the UN is about to choose the successor to incumbent Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, for what many regard as one of the trickiest roles on the world stage. Each term lasts five years, usually renewable for a second term.
The next holder of the post is expected to come from Latin America, given how the post rotates between continents (the last Latin American was Peru’s Javier Perez de Cuellar, who left office in 1992). There is also a long-standing, informal push for the UN to appoint a woman for the first time in its 80-year history.
Whoever wins takes on an organisation under strain from multiple directions. Washington, the UN’s biggest contributor, has cut voluntary funding and withdrawn from the World Health Organization (WHO). Elsewhere, worsening financial pressures and unpaid member state contributions have deepened the ongoing liquidity crisis.
Under Guterres, the UN Security Council has been unable to halt or prevent genocides in Gaza and Sudan, or Russia’s war on Ukraine. Furthermore, the US has committed what many regard as breaches of the charter, including abducting and detaining the president of Venezuela, Nicolás Maduro.
The eight candidates each have their own agenda, but common issues have emerged, including the UN being more proactive to prevent potential crises emerging; the need to be a more streamlined organisation; reducing overlapping functions; allowing smaller nations more opportunity to shake off their debt burdens; and the impact of AI and other technologies on the world.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Syria denies that it met Hezbollah in Turkey
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Syria denies that it met Hezbollah in Turkey
Syria has denied a report from Reuters claiming that its representatives met Hezbollah for face-to-face talks in Turkey last month.
The Reuters report, which cited six sources briefed on events, said that the meeting took place at the invitation of Turkish intelligence agencies in an effort to de-escalate simmering tensions between Syria and the Lebanese paramilitary and political group.
"These claims are false," Syria's foreign media spokesperson wrote on X. "No such meeting took place."
There have been no confirmed meetings between Hezbollah and the Syrian government since the ousting of long-time Hezbollah ally and former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in December 2024.

Egypt condemns Israeli raid at Al-Aqsa
Egypt has condemned raids by Israelis at Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem earlier on Thursday, when hundreds stormed the holy site to mark the sixth day of Sukkot, the Jewish holiday.
Historic status quo agreements governing the shared use of holy sites in Jerusalem and the occupied Palestinian territories reserve Al-Aqsa for Muslim worship, with nearby areas including the Western Wall allocated for Jewish worship.
Members of the Israeli government, including the far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, have on multiple occasions stormed the site, which has long been a flashpoint of tensions between Israelis and Palestinians.
A statement posted by Egypt's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that the raids "exacerbate tensions and threaten the security and stability of the occupied Palestinian territories and the entire region".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Kushner's financial stakes in Israeli defence firms raises conflict of interest concerns: Report
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Kushner's financial stakes in Israeli defence firms raises conflict of interest concerns: Report
US envoy Jared Kushner’s investment firm, Affinity Partners, has the largest stake in an Israeli company invested in more than half a dozen defence companies that have supplied munitions and armaments for the genocide in Gaza and wars on Lebanon, Syria and Iran, according to a report by CNN.
The revelation not only means that Kushner has profited from wars he is officially tapped to negotiate as US President Donald Trump’s envoy, but it means Gulf states including Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar are invested through Kushner’s firm in companies that Israel is using to wage war on Gaza and other Arab states.
Kushner does not have an official position in the US government and is therefore not required to disclose his finances.
Kushner’s link to Israeli defence firms started in 2024 with a $128.5m investment in Phoenix Financial. The company is one of Israel’s largest financial groups, with interests spanning insurance, pensions and asset management. Kushner doubled his stake in Phoenix in January 2025, just five days before Trump was sworn into office. Kushner’s Affinity Partners is Phoenix’s largest shareholder.
CNN found that Phoenix has invested at least $456m in nine companies linked to Israel’s defence sector. Phoenix’s investment in Elbit Systems alone totals at least $265.1m.
